activities.caption: put walking on the pulse scale
activities.name: rtWalkPlace

config.prompt: Humans find pulses easiest between roughly 70 and 180 per minute — the range the body can walk to. Walking sits near what pulse (BPM)?
config.why: Walking sits near 110 — which is why that window dominates popular music: the body's own locomotion range.

activities.anchor: the time signature tells you the tempo
activities.caption: true or false — reading a time signature
activities.name: rtSigJudge

statements.s: The top number counts the grouping and the bottom names the beat unit.
statements.why: 4 = quarter note; the signature says how the counts group.

statements.s: The time signature tells you the tempo.
statements.why: Tempo is a separate decision measured in beats per minute.

statements.s: The same 4/4 can be a march or a power ballad.
statements.why: The signature only says how the counts group — not how fast.

statements.s: 6/8 always means three beats per bar.
statements.why: 6/8 makes two big beats, each splitting into three — the grouping rule, not a headcount of eighths.

activities.anchor: Feel it with the classic spoken pattern
activities.caption: fill the blanks — what swing does to the page
activities.name: rtSwingCloze

config.text: Swing adds a wrinkle: jazz plays pairs of written eighths closer to a triplet (long-short, roughly 2:1), so the page says one thing and the style says another — proof that notation records a %%0%%, not the %%1%%.
config.hint: One word is the bony frame; the other is what moves it.

activities.anchor: A worked transcription shows the arithmetic in action
activities.caption: build the standard rock beat
activities.name: rtBeatOrder

config.prompt: Two rhythms, one grid — order the construction of the standard rock beat:
items: Kick drum on beats 1 and 3 — quarters on the strong heart of the bar
Snare on 2 and 4 — the backbeat, accenting the normally weak beats
Hi-hat on every eighth — eight eighths running under it all
Displace the kick to the 'and' of 3 — the same bar goes funky, one instrument late on purpose, every bar
config.why: Groove is agreements about the grid plus strategic exceptions to it — that is the whole craft.

activities.caption: file each device by its name
activities.name: rtDeviceBuckets

config.prompt: The displacements get their names — file each device:

items.label: reggae's one-drop puts the kick where you least expect it
clap on 2, the 'and' of 3, and 4 — every clap inside the same bar
Scott Joplin's rags shift accents between the hands
in 6/8, grouping the six eighths as 3+3 — a two-beat lilt against the three-beat pattern
Brahms, its great symphonic advocate — three-against-two inside one metre
Ewe drumming interlocking parts over a 12-pulse bell pattern

config.why: Both syncopation and hemiola are the same trick — briefly superimposing one metre on another — which is why the ear hears them as delightful rather than wrong.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the lattice myth
activities.name: rtLatticeSpot

config.prompt: A programme note about West African drumming contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: The parts interlock over a 12-pulse timeline — the bell pattern (3+3+4+2) that acts as a compass everyone navigates by.
Each drummer repeats one simple cycle; the parts meet only on shared downbeats.
The result is an aural mess that only virtuosos can follow.
A listener can lock onto any single line and still feel the whole.
config.correction: The result is a lattice, not a chaos: no single player hears the whole, and the whole is rhythmically richer than any part.
config.why: Each part is simple; the interlock is rich — lock onto any single line and the whole is still there.

activities.anchor: Indian classical music organises time as
activities.caption: call the magnitude — teental's cycle
activities.name: rtTeentalEstimate

config.prompt: Teental — the most common tāla cycle — runs how many beats (mātrās)?
config.why: 16 beats in four groups of four — with accents (tāli), a marked empty beat (khāli), and the return point (sam) where soloist and drummer must land together.
config.context: Other cycles run 7, 10 or 14 — and the Balkans dance in 7/8 grouped 2+2+3.

activities.anchor: Maria Witek's 2014 study found groove ratings peak at medium syncopation
activities.caption: which curve matches the groove finding?
activities.name: rtGrooveTrace

config.prompt: Groove ratings against amount of syncopation — which curve matches what Witek's 2014 study found?
config.why: Groove peaks at medium syncopation — predictable enough to move to, surprising enough to be interesting: pleasure proportional to well-managed error.
